_comment: Block atlas manifest — read at startup by client/src/block_atlas.rs.
This file is the ENTIRE contract between the art set and the engine.
To ship a new set: drop 64x64 PNGs in this folder, then edit `tiles`
(name -> file) and `kinds` (block kind -> which tile each face wears).
No Rust change, no rebuild. `tile_px` may change too, as long as it is
even. Tiles are packed with a wrapped gutter, so every tile must be
SEAMLESS. Face keys: `all` sets top+side+bottom; `top`/`side`/`bottom`
override it.
Art set + hue rationale: see PALETTE.md and docs/material-palette.md
TWO GROUPS of kinds below, and the difference matters:
* hero kinds (plank, floorboard, log, roof_tile, plaster) - addressed by
name from hero.rs / the beauty scene, which builds cube meshes.
* WORLD kinds - named exactly after a sim BlockId (see sim/src/block.rs
`name()`). client/src/voxel.rs looks a block up BY ITS OWN NAME, so a
gameplay block gets file art the moment a kind with its name appears
here, and falls back to the procedural tile when one does not. That is
the whole wiring: no Rust-side alias table to keep in sync.
2026-08-17 second pass: dirt/brick/lamp/red_sand/snow promoted to file art
(all confirmed used by maps/beach_dusk.json + maps/glass_demo.json).
UPDATE 2026-08-18 (Rose): both BlockIds have since landed - WATER=18 and
METAL=19 in sim/src/block.rs::name(), so these two `kinds` entries are now
looked up by real world blocks (maps/river_sunset.json stamps 2011 water
voxels). voxel.rs renders water as a translucent, non-shadow-casting
surface whose top face sits 2/16 below the cube, and METAL is the one
surface-table entry with metallic=1.0 (the loader stamps it into the blue
channel of its `*_r.png`, which is never trusted to carry metalness
itself). They were originally requested by name for the golden-hour
palette; that request is now fulfilled by real blocks.
Blocks still on procedural tiles (no kind here yet): clay, gravel,
cobblestone, obsidian, moss. `stone` currently borrows stone_bricks - it
reads as masonry, not as natural rock; drop a stone_rough.png in and
repoint it when the set grows.
2026-08-18 PBR upgrade (Monanisa): every tile went 16x16 -> 64x64 with
real per-material structure (mortar courses, wood grain fibers, log
rings, individual sand/dirt grains), redrawn from scratch, same HSV
targets as before so the palette didn't move. Each tile entry below also
gained `normal` (<name>_n.png, tangent-space normal map) and `roughness`
(<name>_r.png, grayscale, white=rough/black=mirror-smooth) generated from
a height field authored in the SAME per-pixel pass as the albedo, so the
bump/gloss detail is tied to real drawn structure, not decorrelated
noise. `TileEntry` in block_atlas.rs has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so
these two extra keys are inert until a loader reads them - the render
lane (Poppy) owns wiring PBR sampling into the pipeline. Old 16x16 set
backed up verbatim at assets/textures/blocks_16px_backup/. Generator:
scripts/_pixel_blocks_gen64.py (deterministic, same seeding scheme as
the retired scripts/_pixel_blocks_gen.py).
2026-08-18 environment pack (Monanisa): three additions, generator
scripts/_monanisa_env_pack_gen.py.
(1) `water` was re-authored in place (old speckle-only version backed
up verbatim at assets/textures/blocks/_water_before_repass.png) - the
ripple is now two low-freq directional swell terms domain-warped by a
tileable noise field plus a higher-octave noise chop layer on top (a
first pass using bare integer-frequency sine terms tiled cleanly but
interfered into a visible diagonal argyle lattice at 2x2 zoom; the
noise warp breaks that up while staying exactly period-64), and
roughness is height-coupled instead of a flat override so wave crests
read glossier than troughs. Same HSV target as before (205/0.55/0.55)
- nothing that reads the old hue moves.
(2) 7 vegetation cross-sprites added under `vegetation/` (flower_red,
flower_pink, flower_white, foliage_bush, grass_tall, leaf_birch,
leaf_pine) - RGBA alpha-cutout billboards, NOT full-cube tiles. They
are catalogued below in `tiles` (so load_tiles validates + packs them,
same 64x64 PBR triplet convention) but deliberately have NO `kinds`
entry - there is no cross-quad render mode yet, so a naive `kinds`
wrap would paint them onto all 6 cube faces, which is wrong. Same
ready-but-inert precedent as `water`/`metal` in the first PBR pass:
whoever adds cross-block rendering wires the `kinds` side, no art
change needed then.
(3) sky assets (cloud tile, sunset gradient ramp, sun sprite) are a
different asset family entirely - not blocks, not part of this
manifest - they live at assets/textures/sky/ for the cloud-layer
render code to read directly.
See assets/textures/blocks/PALETTE.md and assets/textures/sky/ for the
full rationale + a combined contact sheet at
assets/textures/env_pack_contact_sheet.png.
2026-08-18 palette-breadth + micro-detail polish (Monanisa): all 19
block tiles above gained a second accent pass answering
docs/art-gap-vs-ceo-ref-2026-08-18.md G6 (6/36 hue bins used vs REF 15)
and G7 (Sobel detail 30.8 vs REF 58.6) - moss/rust/patina/lichen/berry/
wildflower/shell/nail-head accents in a genuinely different hue per
material, not brightness tweaks of the existing hue. No tile_px/atlas
structure change, same 19 file names. Old set backed up verbatim at
assets/textures/blocks_64px_prepolish_backup/. Generator:
scripts/_pixel_blocks_gen64_v3_palette.py (imports _pixel_blocks_gen64.py
for the base layer). Full rationale + before/after table per material:
PALETTE.md; before/after contact sheet:
assets/textures/blocks/contact_sheet_v3_palette.png.
2026-08-20 (Kevin): the 7 vegetation sprites now DO have a `kinds` entry,
each with "mode": "cross" - the cross-quad render mode wired by foliage.rs
(FoliageMaterial). scene.rs's scatter reads these; a naive cube wrap no longer applies.
2026-08-20 realism pass (Monanisa): brick, grass_top, grass_side, leaves,
dirt, sand, water regenerated for material readability (CEO: 'not realistic,
worse than Minecraft'). Two separate root causes: (1) grass_top/grass_side/
leaves came from a Gaussian-blurred-noise generator with no per-texel
structure and s_mean 0.84-0.87 (near-neon) - rewritten as a seamless
toroidal cellular clump field (anisotropic nearest-seed, wraps exactly, no
sine-sum artifact class) at realistic saturation. (2) dirt/sand/water kept
their good per-texel base layer but v4's accent pass stacked 4-5 blobs at
radius 6-16px/max_blend 1.0, covering up to half the tile in flat accent
colour - accent radius/blend cut back to the same restrained scale that
already worked on stone_bricks/oak_planks. Generator:
scripts/_monanisa_realism_pass.py. Tiling verified both visually (2x2
zoom) and statistically (wrap-edge pixel-diff distribution vs interior,
same test class as the tile-zoom-check skill). Before/after:
docs/texture-realism-pass-before-after-2026-08-20.png. Same file names,
same atlas entries - no Rust change, no rebuild. cobblestone/gravel
requested alongside this pass are still procedural-only (no `kinds` entry
yet, no map stamps them) - out of scope here, flagged as a fast-follow.
2026-08-20 material-lock pass (Monanisa): the realism pass above claimed
stone_bricks/oak_planks' accent radius 'already worked' - CEO screenshot
showed that was wrong. Real root cause: scatter_blobs(exclude=fn) only
gates the blob CENTER, paint_blobs() then paints the full radius (up to
16px) regardless - every accent 'restricted to mortar/seam' still bled
deep into the material face. oak_planks/oak_log_side had NO exclude at
all. Fixed oak_planks, oak_log_side, oak_log_top, brick, stone_bricks,
dirt, sand: replaced radius-based accents with masked_speckle() (gates
every texel individually, cannot overshoot a mask) for anything meant to
stay inside a thin geometric feature (mortar groove, plank seam, bark
crack), kept small paint_blobs() only for genuinely round features
(wood knots) in material-family hues, and pulled dirt/sand accent hues
back into their own family (was h=352 pink + h=115 green on dirt, two
stacked teal sources at h=172/174 on sand). Verified 0% green/teal/pink
pixel share on all 6 (stone_bricks keeps an intentional thin olive moss
film confined to its mortar groove, ~26% of groove pixels, 0% of the
stone face). Generator: scripts/_monanisa_material_lock_pass.py.
Before/after: docs/evidence/material-lock-2026-08-20/.
